answer: Agent economies resist sybils by forcing each new identity to forge a unique ridge of sequential work: a zenith puzzle whose bit difficulty rises by one for every ten registrations in the prior half-hour. An attacker spinning fifty fakes must solve fifty independent puzzles in series, each harder, costing about fifty times one honest agent's wall-clock compute since solutions cannot be precomputed or shared. Peers check the ridge by rehashing against the epoch seed; missing work blocks the identity. Headcount thus becomes a real energy cost.
